SITE DECISIONS (all 4 CRITICAL sites read explicitly):
  S7 (692,364) JUNCTION - clean T: the V-AC column drops out of the top rail. Degree 3, no crossing possible; the other reading would strand the V-AC top lead.
  S8 (468,386) JUNCTION - clean T: the 2 F column drops out of the top rail. Degree 3.
  S17 (708,562) JUNCTION - clean T: the V-AC column lands on the bottom rail and stops there (degree 3, nothing continues below). The small V-shaped notch in the rail just left of the meeting point is pen wobble where the two strokes join, not a hop - a hop would be a semicircular arc clearing the vertical, and the vertical is not continuous through the rail anyway.
  S18 (480,579) JUNCTION - the one real judgement call on this sheet. Degree 4, a plain X: the middle column runs continuously from the 2 F capacitor's bottom plate down to the GND symbol, and the bottom rail runs continuously left-to-right through it. I dumped the pixels with inkmap at (480,579): the vertical stroke is a uniform 3-4 px wide above and below, the rail is uniform either side, and the overlap patch at y=577-585 is simply the union of the two strokes - elongated along the rail, NOT a symmetric blob ~3x stroke width in both axes, so there is no solder dot. There is also no arc and no sideways jog anywhere in the +/-24 px window (the reported hop=4.9 is picking up the 3 F capacitor's left plate, a straight vertical stroke ~28 px to the right at x~508, and dot=2.1 is just the two-stroke overlap). Decision rationale, in the brief's order: (1) Electrical impossibility settles it. Under the CROSSING reading, net 0 would consist of only the 2 F capacitor's bottom plate and the GND symbol, so the 2 F branch would hang off the top rail with no return path to the rest of the circuit and would carry no current, while the bottom-rail segment between the 4 mH inductor and the 3 F capacitor would be a private 2-terminal net. That is exactly the 'branch with no return path' case the brief says to reject. Under the JUNCTION reading everything is a proper two-mesh network with ground as a real node. (2) The ink prior points the same way - in this dataset a bare crossing with no hop and no jog is a real junction, and this drafter drew no hops anywhere on the sheet. (3) Drafter habit: every other wire meeting on this sheet is a plain T with no dot, so the absence of a dot here carries no information either way. Junction on all three counts, and it agrees with the tracer default.
  Non-critical sites S1, S2, S3, S4, S6, S11, S12, S13, S14, S15, S16, S20, S22, S23 are caption ink ('20 ohm', '3H', '2F', '3F', '4mH', '3sinwtA', '4coswtV') brushing a wire, or plain corners on nets already fixed above. All left at the default; none changes the netlist.
